**Chinese name:** 豪威集成电路（集团）股份有限公司 (Háowēi Jíchéng Diànlù (Jítuán) Gǔfèn Yǒuxiàn Gōngsī)

::: {.callout-tip}
## Why This Matters
OmniVision Technologies (originally a US company) was acquired by a Chinese consortium led by Will Semiconductor in 2019; the parent formally renamed itself from Will Semiconductor (韦尔股份) to OmniVision Group (豪威集团/豪威集成电路（集团）股份有限公司) and pursued a Hong Kong IPO — a notable case of a Chinese fabless firm acquiring a once-independent Western chip brand outright rather than building one from scratch. Unlike most other entries updated in this tracker's 2026 sweep, OmniVision's recent results moved the other direction: Q1 2026 net profit fell 41.9% YoY to ¥503 million, and H1 2026 net profit fell 39.9% YoY to ¥1.22 billion — a useful reminder that China's chip sector is not uniformly booming even where AI/memory-linked names are. 2025 full-year net profit had been reported up ~498% YoY to ¥3.3 billion, making the 2026 decline a reversal from an unusually strong prior-year base rather than a new structural problem, though this tracker has not independently confirmed which explanation is correct.
:::

## What does this firm design?

CMOS image sensors (smartphone and automotive cameras), plus analog and display driver solutions.
